context: A teacher walks a uni student through a public-health & politics paper
purpose: Teach: 引き起こし/妨げ/党首/幕府/中傷/ワクチン/肺/上空

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 論文、ワクチン政策と党首発言の関係を扱うんですね。
lines.en: Your paper examines vaccine policy and party-leader statements, then.
lines.style: Warm interest—not interrogative but invitational. Steady pace. Slight lift on the period word, drawing him in. Genuinely curious about his angle, not checking off a requirement.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。誤情報が肺疾患の早期発見を妨げた事例も含めます。
lines.en: Yes. I'm also including cases where misinformation delayed early detection of lung disease.
lines.style: Quiet resolve. Speaks carefully, aware he's introducing something heavier. Steady eye contact. Not rushed, but purposeful—this matters and he knows it.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 歴史的には、幕府期の流言が同様の混乱を引き起こした例もあります。
lines.en: Historically, rumors during the shogunate period caused similar kinds of confusion.
lines.style: Leaning forward slightly. Warm—offering a bridge, not a lecture. Pacing deliberately to let the parallel land. The tone of someone who sees his thinking and wants to deepen it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 中傷の拡散経路、上空からの俯瞰図のように整理します。
lines.en: I'll organize the pathways of slander-spread like a bird's-eye map.
lines.style: Concrete and visual. Slight pick-up in energy—he's found his structure. Not defensive, but confident in the method. Clean consonants on the key words.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.style: Gentle but firm. Not a warning—a gift of permission to slow down. Brief, because it needs to land lightly. Warm undertone that says she trusts him to do this right.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.style: Small, sincere acknowledgment. No performance. A quiet nod in the voice—the kind that says he heard not just the words but what was underneath them.
